extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, reviewing officers, military commanders, and military-law practitioners responsible for court-martial proceedings and review
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and legal criteria for the conduct, recordation, review, approval, disapproval, and execution of court-martial findings and sentences under military law. Focuses on what defects are material, when proceedings/sentences must be disapproved or may be corrected, and proper recording/authentication practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: There is always a presumption, in the absence of obvious irregularity, that the proceedings were regular and according to law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless an irregularity is obvious, proceedings will be presumed regular; reviewer should look for clear defects before disapproving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lost or destroyed record renders proceedings inoperative
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the record of the trial was lost or destroyed before review so that proceedings cannot be intelligently reviewed or formally approved, the proceedings should be considered inoperative and the sentence of no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If practicable the record should be returned to the court for correction; complete destruction (by fire, loss of stenographic notes, etc.) may operate as an acquittal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misnaming/misdescription of rank — objection by plea in abatement
rubrics_metrics.description: A misnaming or misdescription of the rank of the accused in the specification should be taken advantage of by exception in the nature of a plea in abatement; where not objected to, the error is immaterial after sentence provided the accused is sufficiently identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If objected to at the appropriate time, amendment should be directed; failure to object generally waives defect post-sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical spelling errors (idem sonans) not material
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere clerical error in the spelling of the name of the accused, leaving it idem sonans, is not a case of misnomer and does not affect the validity of the proceedings as recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small spelling variants that are phonetic equivalents do not invalidate proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission or indefiniteness of time/place — amend if objected
rubrics_metrics.description: Where time or place is omitted to be averred, or is averred without sufficient definiteness, and the defect is excepted to by the accused on being called to plead, the court will properly direct that an amendment be made. But where no objection is interposed, proceedings will be sufficient if time and place can be made out with reasonable certainty from the testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Object early to preserve defect; absent objection, review looks to whether testimony supplies reasonable certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in article numbering immaterial absent objection
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges laid under old article numbers (using old numbers instead of new) are errors which can only be taken advantage of by an objection in the nature of a plea in abatement and are immaterial after finding and sentence if not objected to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural numbering mistakes are curable by amendment if timely objected to; otherwise generally waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal hostility of judge advocate does not void proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that the judge advocate was personally objectionable or hostile to the accused could not affect the validity of the proceedings of a court-martial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal animus of prosecuting officer, absent other legal defects, does not by itself invalidate proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confinement/physical condition (shackles) not necessarily fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: That an accused soldier was tried with hands or feet in shackles, or with ball-and-chain attached, omitted to be removed during the hearing, does not affect the legality of the proceedings or sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although reprehensible, use of shackles during hearing does not automatically invalidate; consider prejudice to accused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member acting as interpreter — irregularity not necessarily fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: That a member of the court acted as interpreter on a trial is an irregularity, but one which did not affect the legality of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irregularities of role may be tolerable unless shown to have caused prejudice; some role conflicts (see prosecuting witness-as-interpreter) are more serious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter/clerk privy to finding/sentence not fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial member, judge advocate, or others cannot lawfully communicate the finding or sentence to a reporter or clerk before deliberation; the court should require such persons to withdraw. But the fact that the finding or sentence may have been made known to the reporter or clerk cannot affect legality of proceedings or sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: require withdrawal; but prior disclosure to clerical personnel does not automatically invalidate proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjournment notation not essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting the adjournment of the court at end of the record is usual and proper, but a statement of such adjournment is not an essential part of the record and its omission will not affect legality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative notations helpful but not jurisdictional defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal record = that approved and authenticated by court
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal record is that record which is finally approved and adopted by the court as a body and authenticated by its president and judge advocate; it is immaterial who actually wrote or kept it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the court's formal approval/authentication rather than the identity of the scribe; corrections and final approval by the court are dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review weight for courts' credibility assessments in conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: In passing upon findings and sentence, the reviewing officer will properly attach special weight to the court's conclusions where testimony has been of a conflicting character because the court saw the witnesses and their manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should defer to factfinding when credibility judgments are central, absent clear error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence must rest on an approved finding of guilty
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence, to be valid, must rest upon an approved finding of guilty of an offense for which the accused was tried; a duly approved finding on one charge which authorizes the sentence may validate the sentence even if other findings disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review that at least one approved finding legally supports the sentence; if sentence disproportionate to that finding, mitigation or correction may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding guilty of specification but not charge insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: A finding of guilty of a specification to a charge but not guilty of the charge itself will not support a sentence unless there is added a conviction of some lesser offense included in that charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical distinctions between charge and specification matter; ensure the legal basis for any sentence is present in approved findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of summons for clearly material witness is ground for disapproval
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a good ground for disapproval of a sentence that the court denied the accused's request to have summoned a clearly material and important witness whose testimony would not have been merely cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality and non-cumulativeness of omitted witness testimony are key to finding prejudice warranting disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of member at revision who was absent during original trial illegal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a member absent during the whole of the original proceedings is in fact present during proceedings had on revision to reconsider the sentence, the revised sentence is clearly illegal and should be disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members who did not hear evidence should not participate in revision deliberations; their presence at revision invalidates revised action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material name variance between specification and sentence fatal unless corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: A material variance between the name of the accused in the specification and in the sentence should, if possible, be corrected by reassembling the court for revision; if impracticable the sentence should in general be disapproved as fatally defective. Differences in middle initial are not material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish material variances (completely different names or non- idem-sonans) from immaterial initials; correct via court reassembly if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecuting witness acting as interpreter is grave irregularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the charges were preferred by an officer who acted as a prosecuting witness and also as interpreter, this is a grave irregularity which might induce disapproval unless it clearly appears no injustice was done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts of role involving prosecutorial witness+interpreter are serious; unless harmless beyond doubt, expect disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reentry of absent member permissible with communication of omitted proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not invalidate proceedings that a member present during part then absented himself and later resumed his seat; nor is adding a new member during trial invalid, provided testimony and material proceedings which occurred while absent are communicated to him before he resumes duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication of missing testimony is required to cure absence; substantial absence may still justify disapproval if prejudice likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial absence of member may induce disapproval
rubrics_metrics.description: A member who has been absent during a substantial part of a trial returning to take part in conviction and sentence is a marked irregularity and may well induce disapproval where there's reason to believe accused suffered material disadvantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether absence was substantial and whether prejudice to accused resulted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate cannot be substituted by junior member; role conflict fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: An order convening that if the judge advocate be prevented from attending the junior member will act in his stead is irregular and improper; a member having acted both as judge advocate and member should prompt disapproval of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge advocate's prosecutorial function is incompatible with being a member; court must not empower members to act as judge advocate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness may generally correct testimony; refusal not fatal absent prejudice
rubrics_metrics.description: A witness who has given testimony should in general be allowed to modify the same materially; refusal by the court to permit correction need not induce disapproval unless it appears rights of the accused were prejudiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether refusal to permit correction caused prejudice to accused's defense before disapproving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentences exceeding regulatory solitary-confinement limits unauthorized
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence prescribing solitary confinement in excess of the proportion fixed by Army Regulations is unauthorized and should be disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare sentence terms to controlling regulations (e.g., annual solitary confinement caps); excessive terms invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence must clearly indicate confinement duration
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence which, in imposing confinement, fails clearly to indicate how long the same is to continue is irregular and inoperative and should be disapproved unless corrected by reassembling the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous duration destroys enforceability; prefer correction by court reassembly where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegating discharge date to reviewing officer illegal
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial sentencing a soldier to be dishonorably discharged at such date as might be fixed by the reviewing officer is illegal, as devolving upon the reviewing officer a duty pertaining to the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts must fix the effective date of punishments reserved to their judgment; reviewers cannot be given authority to set essential elements of sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions/substitutions that negate material allegation invalidate finding
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court makes such exceptions and substitutions in its finding upon a specification as to negative the material allegation (e.g., false writing), there is no legal basis for the finding of guilty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the finding actually embraces the material elements of the offense; alterations that remove those elements render the finding baseless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompatible findings across articles (desertion vs. other offenses) not allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: A finding of not guilty of desertion but guilty of a violation of another article (e.g., 40th) under the same charge is not allowable and should be disapproved where the lesser offense is not necessarily included in the greater charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check statutory/technical inclusions: lesser must be legally 'included' in charge to support substitute finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court jurisdiction may end with cessation of hostilities (58th article cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: If peace is declared before charges under the fifty-eighth article of war are brought to trial or before sentence imposed, the court is without jurisdiction and the sentence is illegal and should be set aside; if peace declared before record reaches reviewing authority he cannot legally act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional effect of state of war/peace is dispositive for certain articles; reviewer must verify temporal jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Less punishment under certain war-articles than local law illegal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the court awarded a less punishment under the fifty-eighth article than that prescribed for the offense by local law, the sentence was illegal and inoperative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare military sentence to applicable local law in occupation/hostile jurisdiction contexts; cannot undercut local penal prescription where law requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles prescribing dismissal forbid additional punishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Under articles that prescribe dismissal upon conviction, no punishment in addition to dismissal is authorized; all additional punishments should be disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When statute prescribes a sole penalty, avoid adding fines, confinement, etc.; such additions are illegal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to assert challenge or improper ruling generally does not void proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: That a sufficient cause of challenge exists but, through ignorance of rights, is not taken advantage of by the accused, or if asserted is improperly overruled by the court, does not affect the validity in law of the proceedings or sentence though it may furnish occasion for disapproval or remission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver doctrines apply; lack of timely objection usually precludes automatic reversal but may justify equitable relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of continuance despite reasonable cause may be ground for disapproval
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reasonable cause is exhibited in the judgment of the court, the party is entitled to some continuance under article 93; refusal will not invalidate proceedings per se but may be good ground for disapproving the sentence or mitigating/pardoning if accused prejudiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prejudice from denial of continuance; presence of reasonable cause creates entitlement to relief if prejudicial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penitentiary confinement for purely military offenses unauthorized
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence of penitentiary confinement in a case of a purely military offense is wholly unauthorized and should be disapproved; it cannot be made effective by commuting from a severer penalty (e.g., death) to penitentiary confinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure punishments correspond to the statutory range for the offense; civilian penitentiary sentences are improper for purely military offenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and nature of disapproval by reviewing officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Disapproval of the sentence by the legal reviewing authority quite nullifies it; disapproval is a final determinate act putting an end to the proceedings in that case and preventing accruing disabilities incident upon approval. To be operative, a disapproval should be express; mere absence of approval is not disapproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must expressly disapprove to nullify; merely refraining from approval or forwarding without words of approval is not the same as disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer cannot disapprove then mitigate/commute
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewing officer cannot disapprove a sentence and then proceed to mitigate or commute the punishment, since upon disapproval there is nothing left to act upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewer intends to mitigate, must not formally disapprove; procedural sequence matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disapproval of finding = acquittal; disapproval of acquittal ineffective
rubrics_metrics.description: Disapproval of a finding of guilty has the effect of an acquittal. Conversely, formal disapproval by reviewing authority of an acquittal is a naked nonconcurrence and is without legal effect; the accused remains legally not guilty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disapproving a conviction equates to acquittal; reviewers cannot convert acquittal to conviction by mere disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisible sentences exceeding legal limit may be partially approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a sentence in excess of the legal limit is divisible, such part as is legal may be approved and executed (e.g., fines beyond statutory limit: approve lawful portion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, salvage and execute lawful portions rather than invalidating entire divisible punishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolonged pretrial arrest or awaiting promulgation may mitigate punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: That a soldier has been held in arrest for an unreasonably protracted period before trial or while awaiting promulgation of sentence is good ground for mitigation of punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider duration of pretrial/detention when weighing mitigation or remission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation for provocation or excessive force by officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where mutiny or other misconduct was provoked by inexcusable violence or recklessness of an officer, severe punishments (even death) should be mitigated and the officer brought to trial; sentences of long imprisonment for momentary provoked conduct have often been mitigated or disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual mitigation recommended where superior misconduct induced accused's conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review action may be recalled before publication but not after notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken by a reviewing officer upon proceedings and sentence may be recalled and modified before it is published and the party notified; after such notice the action is beyond recall and an approval cannot be substituted for a disapproval or vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of notice/publication fixes finality; reviewers should ensure correctness before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of confirmed dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: When a legal sentence of dismissal has been legally confirmed and executed, the reviewing officer's power over the case is exhausted; the act of confirmation is functus officio and, as an executive act, the dismissal is final and irreversible so far as Executive power is concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After lawful confirmation/execution of dismissal, the only recourse is new appointment; the reviewing authority cannot revoke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer may designate penitentiary within command
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a soldier is sentenced to confinement in a penitentiary, the reviewing officer within his command may designate a particular penitentiary as the place of confinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer's designation must be consistent with offense and sentence; consideration of command boundaries applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on changing designated place of confinement
rubrics_metrics.description: If sentence directs confinement at hard labor 'in such place as the reviewing authority may direct,' the reviewing authority may designate a penitentiary; but if he designates a military post as the place of confinement, the place cannot, pending its execution at the post, legally be changed to a penitentiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial designation controls pending execution; later substitution to a more severe penal environment is constrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of place of confinement for service exigencies allowed if no harsher confinement imposed
rubrics_metrics.description: It is authorized to change the place of confinement of a prisoner if required by exigencies of the service, provided that no more severe species of confinement than that contemplated in the sentence is enforced after the transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers permitted for logistical reasons but must preserve the nature/degree of confinement ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprimand severity discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a reprimand is generally intended as mild punishment, its quality is left to the discretion of the authority pronouncing it and may be made as severe as he deems expedient without being chargeable with adding to the punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprimands are flexible; assess severity within discretionary bounds, not considered an added punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of reviewing action in record
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should exhibit, at the end of the proceedings, the action thereon — approval or disapproval — of the reviewing authority; this should be written and signed within the record for each trial rather than merely annexed or indorsed on the last of a series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper practice: write and subscribe action within each case record; forwarding with vague references like 'referred for action' is incomplete and irregular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority should authenticate by handwritten signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing authority should authenticate action by subscribing in his own hand (adding rank and command) the official statement written in or upon the record; impressing the signature by stamp is not favored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handwritten signature with rank/command best evidence of authority and authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release pending review for acquittal or non-confinement sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: When a trial results in an acquittal or when the sentence does not contain confinement, the prisoner may, pending review of the proceedings, be released from confinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orderly release pending review is appropriate where sentence/acquittal justify it; ensure proper documentation.
